target_customer: Families arranging a funeral (consumers), with funeral homes as a secondary paying channel
problem: Families face an average funeral cost of about $9,000 under emotional stress, with no single place to raise funds, compare vendors and coordinate the community of the deceased.
business_model: Marketplace and lead generation for funeral homes and vendors, plus a free fundraising and memorial tool for families
product_category: Funeral planning marketplace and memorial fundraising

founders.name: Alison Johnston
founders.background_notes: Background per TechCrunch March 2019. Education not found in a source I opened.

founders.name: Eric Zarowny
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page; no background found.

competitors.name: Funeral360
competitors.what: Online funeral planning and booking, described by TechCrunch as the biggest rival

competitors.name: FuneralWise
competitors.what: Funeral education content and forums with limited booking and no memorial site builder

competitors.name: Service Corporation International
competitors.what: Large public funeral operator that owns many funeral homes

technical_complexity.rationale: A marketplace, directory and fundraising web app; the hard part was assembling funeral home and vendor data and trust, not engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Directory and fundraising features were copyable by general crowdfunding sites; a vendor directory with reviews gives only a weak data moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought or clearly copied it in the sources I found; GoFundMe offered memorial-specific fundraising formats.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in March 2019 cited an average funeral cost near $9,000 and families struggling to organize money and vendors, with online fundraising already used for funerals.

branding.domain_note: Uses everloved.com; acquisition history not found.

identity.logo: not described in sources I found
identity.voice_and_tone: Warm, supportive language aimed at grieving families

branding.community_and_virality: Memorial pages are shared among family and friends, but no source describes brand-level virality.

brand_strength.rationale: A gentle, memorable name fitting the emotional category, and press coverage (TechCrunch 2019, Freethink), but no source shows the brand itself driving growth.

outcome_analysis: Ever Loved is still operating and sells to funeral homes by sending families to them, with the founder bringing two earlier exits. Funding is small and only a Social Capital led seed is confirmed, so the company looks like a steady niche business rather than a breakout, and no layoffs, sale or shutdown were found.
notes: Seed amount not disclosed by TechCrunch. CB Insights (aggregator) reports a $1.5M seed in September 2019 and $1.65M total with AltaIR Capital, Bossa Invest and Coughdrop Capital; one other aggregator lists a $25K seed in 2024. These are unverified and not recorded as rounds. Everloved.com blocked fetch (403). Outcome search found no shutdown or sale; a 2025 article indicates it is still operating. Competition from Cake, Everplans or Lantern not confirmed.
